subject.title: feat(gateway): wire read coding tool into HTTP /tools/invoke (narrow)

question: Should OpenClaw core expose its built-in host-filesystem `read` tool through Gateway direct invocation when `gateway.tools.allow`, `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead`, and owner/admin identity all pass?
rationale: The code can enforce the proposed gate, but only maintainers can decide whether this authenticated host-data access capability is an acceptable core security and product boundary.

options.title: Accept the narrow owner-gated read capability
options.body: Approve the default-off three-part gate, then require an exact-head rebase and focused fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Keep host reads outside core direct invocation
options.body: Decline this new Gateway capability and leave direct tool invocation limited to existing supported surfaces or external extensions.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow owner-gated read capability
recommendation.body: Approve the default-off three-part gate, then require an exact-head rebase and focused fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion directly routes the Gateway boundary decision to this person.
